articles.title: Why Josh Simmons Was Told to Leave Meeting by Mahomes, Reid Revealed in New Chiefs Rumors
articles.summary: A tense exchange between Josh Simmons and head coach Andy Reid preceded the Kansas City Chiefs placing the second-year offensive tackle on injured reserve, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
A tense exchange between Josh Simmons and head coach Andy Reid preceded the Kansas City Chiefs placing the second-year offensive tackle on injured reserve, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport .

On Wednesday, Simmons "was sitting with his feet up in the offense's meeting room when Reid asked him to put his feet down."

"Simmons pushed back by telling Reid he had to sit that way because his back and hips were aching, according to sources, per Garafolo and Rapoport. "Reid then instructed Simmons to get treatment from the athletic trainers if he was indeed in pain."

Biggest takeaways from Bears' win over Patriots

Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes also told Simmons he should leave the meeting.

The 2025 first-round pick exited the room and later apologized to Reid and his teammates.

Kansas City placed Simmons on injured reserve Thursday.

Simmons' rookie season was cut short due to a fractured wrist . A bulging disk in his back has prevented him from suiting up at all in 2026, and his IR designation means he'll be sidelined until at least Week 11.

Chiefs trainer Rick Burkholder told reporters this week the 23-year-old "worked his tail off" in trying to get healthy.

"He worked diligently with my staff every day and has improved to point where he could return to practice in a limited capacity last week," Burkholder said. "However, we feel like he's plateaued in the rehab process as he's trying to get to the final steps of recovery with the return to competition. He's just not there yet."

The Chiefs staked a lot on Simmons. Offensive tackle was one of their biggest positional needs heading into the 2025 NFL draft, and they seemingly addressed that with the former Ohio State standout.

Instead, Kansas City finds itself using Kahlil Benson, an undrafted rookie, as the starting left tackle. That's going to remain the case for four more weeks and perhaps beyond that.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Reveal Every Team Eyeing Colts Star as NFL Landing Spot
articles.summary: At least five teams could be in the market for Jonathan Taylor should the Indianapolis Colts be open to trading the star running back.
articles.body:
At least five teams could be in the market for Jonathan Taylor should the Indianapolis Colts be open to trading the star running back.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday the Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, Minnesota Vikings, and Denver Broncos are likely to "ponder the possibility" of acquiring the three-time Pro Bowler. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday "sources believe the New York Giants and Vikings could be potential suitors."

The Colts are 2-4 and fired general manager Chris Ballard. Their disappointing start has led people to wonder whether they'll wave the white flag for 2026 and begin building for the future.

Taylor is Indianapolis' biggest trade asset if that's a lever the interim front office wants to pull. Finances would be a factor in the decision as well given his salary cap hit in 2027 is $21 million . The number climbs to $23 million in 2028.

Jones pumped the breaks on a deal for now. He reported Indy "needs to see what the landscape is like in a few weeks before deciding on its star running back."

Taylor's 4.0 yards per carry are on pace to be a career low, but he has still logged the second-most carries in the league while running for 492 yards and seven touchdowns. A week ago, he went for 94 yards and a score in a 26-20 loss to the Tennessee Titans.

Give Taylor more support in the passing game — the Colts are averaging 199.8 yards per contest through the air — and his numbers might improve a bit.

The Packers are an interesting team to have the veteran ball-carrier on their radar.

Green Bay just activated Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list, and he's under contract for one more year. If general manager Brian Gutekunst were to do something as bold as trade for Taylor, most would probably assume Jacobs is on the way out before the 2027 season.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, have a Kenneth Walker III-sized void in their backfield. Maybe first-round pick Jadarian Price becomes a viable long-term successor, but the rookie remains on injured reserve.

Adding Taylor to the mix would undoubtedly improve Seattle's running game right now but would present some questions about where Price fits into the picture.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill’s custody battle heats up as  court demand to reveal how much time he spends with his 10 children
articles.summary: Tyreek Hill’s ongoing divorce battle has entered another sensitive phase, with his estranged wife, Keeta Vaccaro, seeking records that could shed light on
articles.body: Tyreek Hill’s ongoing divorce battle has entered another sensitive phase, with his estranged wife, Keeta Vaccaro, seeking records that could shed light on his role as a father. The Miami-Dade court filing asks the NFL star to provide documents showing how much time he has spent with his 10 children over the past several months. The request comes shortly after a jury ordered Hill to pay Vaccaro $500,000 in a battery case. With parenting arrangements still unresolved, the records could become important in determining how the former couple handles custody and shared parenting responsibilities.Tyreek Hill must provide parenting records in divorce caseVaccaro submitted her request on October 16, asking Hill to produce an existing parenting plan and records of his time-sharing arrangements from May 6 onward. She wants documents that could help establish when Hill spent time with his children and how often those visits took place.The requested materials include calendars, personal agendas, travel receipts and flight itineraries. Hill has 30 days from the date he received the request to respond, placing his deadline in mid-November.The filing could offer a clearer picture of the practical side of parenting while the divorce proceedings continue. Although financial disputes and allegations of misconduct have attracted attention, custody and time-sharing remain major unresolved issues between the couple.Hill and Vaccaro's marriage began in November 2023, but their relationship later deteriorated. Their divorce case started in April 2025, following a domestic dispute that prompted a police response in Sunny Isles Beach.The latest demand does not establish how much time Hill has spent with his children. Instead, it seeks documentation that could help clarify the situation as the legal proceedings move forward.$500,000 battery verdict adds pressure on Tyreek HillThe request for parenting records follows a jury's decision to find Hill liable on two battery counts while rejecting eight other counts. The verdict ordered him to pay Vaccaro $500,000.During the trial, testimony covered their relationship, financial disagreements and footage recorded by a nanny camera. Vaccaro and her mother, Alicia Vaccaro, also testified. A therapist's diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder formed part of the proceedings.Hill, meanwhile, raised allegations about the couple's finances. He testified that Vaccaro took around $60,000 per month without his permission, in addition to a $15,000 monthly allowance. He said the disputes began before their wedding and described his reaction during one disagreement."I got furious. I'm like, 'Babe, why are you stealing money? Like, all you got to do is just say, Hey, Reek, like help me out,'" Hill said in testimony.The jury's verdict and Vaccaro's latest filing represent separate developments in the wider dispute. Hill also remains under review by the NFL under its Personal Conduct Policy.For now, the next significant step is Hill's response to the document request. The records could become relevant as the court addresses the outstanding questions surrounding custody and parenting time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Chiefs OT Josh Simmons kicked out of meeting by Andy Reid, Patrick Mahomes before going on IR
articles.summary: Josh Simmons has not played this season due to a back injury.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive tackle Josh Simmons was reportedly kicked out of a team meeting by Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes prior to being placed on injured reserve, according to NFL Network. The incident occurred Wednesday. A day later, Simmons was put on IR.

During a Wednesday team meeting, Simmons was reportedly sitting with his feet up. Chiefs coach Andy Reid asked Simmons to put his feet down, to which Simmons reportedly responded that his back and hips were bothering him and he had to sit that way. Reid then told Simmons to go receive treatment if he was hurting.

The pair continued to discuss the issue until Patrick Mahomes also told Simmons to leave and go get treatment. The 23-year-old offensive lineman did leave the room, though stayed at Chiefs' facilities.

Later that day, Simmons apologized to Reid and Chiefs leadership, per NFL Network.

Simmons, who the team selected in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, has not played this season due to a back injury. He appeared to be on the mend, however, and was able to put in limited practices ahead of Week 6. Despite that, he was ruled out for the contest.

On Wednesday, Simmons was unable to practice due to the issue. He was listed on the injury report due to back and personal reasons. With Simmons' back once again acting up, the team gave Simmons a day to speak with his family and representation about his next steps. The next day, the team placed Simmons on injured reserve, ensuring he'll miss the next four games as he recovers from the injury.

Simmons initially complained of a calf issue in August. After being looked at by trainers, it was believed Simmons was dealing with a bulging disk in his back, which an MRI later confirmed. Doctors recommended rehab over surgery for Simmons. When the team did imaging following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, the disk looked better, resulting in Simmons returning to practice.

But the injury was still giving Simmons trouble ahead of Week 7, leading to the lineman being placed on IR.

Simmons was selected by the team to be a blindside protector for Mahomes, one of the most important jobs in football. But the second-year player has played in only eight games due to injuries and personal absences. He missed multiple weeks as a rookie due to personal reasons and then sustained a fractured wrist in Week 13. He was later placed on IR, ending his season.

With Simmons' latest injury, the offensive lineman will be eligible to return in Week 11 at the earliest. With Simmons out, the Chiefs have relied on undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson at left tackle.

articles.title: Puka Nacua Injured, Latest Updates on Rams WR with Davante Adams on IR
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua left the team's practice with a calf injury Thursday, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop. However, the Rams are optimistic Nacua will play in Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams wideout Puka Nacua left the team's practice with a calf injury Thursday, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop . However, the Rams are optimistic Nacua will play in Sunday's matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

"Nacua, who is listed as questionable because of a calf injury, was feeling better Saturday, according to the source, who said: 'As long as there aren't any setbacks, we feel good about him being available to play,' according to Schefter. "Nacua underwent an MRI on his calf Thursday that came back better than the Rams had hoped, sources said. He did not practice Friday."

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, the injury is believed to be "minor."

"My understanding is, after the tests, it was more minor than anything else," Rapoport said on Friday. "I wouldn't say precautionary, because it's not nothing, but at least not a significant injury."

Cornerback Trent McDuffie and linebacker Nate Landman are both questionable and didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday. Defensive lineman Myles Garrett, Poona Ford and Kobie Turner, wideout Davante Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson are all on injured reserve. Kicker Blake Grupe is out for the season with a torn ACL.

The Rams came into the season with Super Bowl aspirations but has instead started 2-4 and risks falling out of the playoff picture altogether if it can't start stringing some wins together.

Health has been a concern for the young wideout in his career:

The 25-year-old already missed two games this season but has been fantastic when healthy, catching 37 passes on 52 targets for 417 yards and a touchdown. He's also rushed for a touchdown.

That Nacua leads the team in receptions and targets despite missing two games is an excellent reminder of how incredibly valuable he is to quarterback Matthew Stafford and the team's offense. Being without him against a scrappy Raiders team that's seeking to end a three-game losing streak would leave Los Angeles in fairly dire straits on both sides of the ball.

articles.title: New Peyton Manning Rumors on Colts GM Job and 'Any NFL Opportunities' After Chris Ballard's Firing
articles.summary: NFL legend Peyton Manning wears a lot of hats these days. General manager of the Indianapolis Colts won't be one of them.
articles.body:
NFL legend Peyton Manning wears a lot of hats these days. General manager of the Indianapolis Colts won't be one of them.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday the Colts "have not approached Manning about their vacant GM job, nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position."

According to Schefter, Manning isn't prepared to assume the kind of time requirement being an NFL GM would demand. He's not closing the door altogether on working inside the league, though:

"Manning would be willing to listen and consider any NFL opportunities at any time, but the Colts have not discussed any of those possibilities with him, according to sources. It's possible that some could come in the future, sources said, but those discussions likely would involve higher-profile positions similar to the ones that other former NFL quarterbacks have accepted with other franchises."

Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon announced Monday the team was dismissing general manager Chris Ballard. A 26-20 loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans was the final straw.

Almost immediately, Dan Patrick reported on his radio show that Manning could be a factor in the search for a new GM:

Mike Chappell of Fox 59 in Indianapolis followed up on that to cast doubt on the retired star making a transition to the front office:

Manning has long been floated as a possible general manager one day. As far back as 2019, former teammate Reggie Wayne suggested he might one day be a "new, modern Jerry Jones" in that he'd share the titles of owner and GM.

Jason La Canfora reported for CBS Sports in 2021 that Manning was interested in possibly purchasing a stake in the Denver Broncos and "already had discussions with several of the groups expected to be favorites to land the team."

Alas, here we are in 2026 and the 50-year-old is no closer to occupying an official role on a team. He appears content to be a commercial pitchman and widen his television footprint through his Omaha Productions studio.

articles.title: NFL Week 7 Live Fantasy Football Start 'Em Sit 'Em Lineup Advice and Latest Injury Updates
articles.summary: We're only just now about to hit the halfway point of the fantasy football regular season. But we are 100 percent of the way to wacky-land already—because 2026 has been a year y'all.

OK, so starting Bo Nix in Week 7 straddles the line between brave and dumb--the Broncos quarterback has been dreadful in recent weeks.

But as Raza Umerani wrote at NFL.com , if ever there was a week for Nix to get going, this is it.

If there were ever a time to Bo-lieve, it's now."

articles.title: Eagles Under Investigation over Jalen Hurts' Blood Clots, NFL and NFLPA Confirm in Joint Statement
articles.summary: The NFL and the National Football League Players Association released a joint statement Sunday revealing there will be an investigation into how the Philadelphia Eagles handled Jalen Hurts' blood clot situation during and around the team's Week 5 trip to London to play the Jacksonville Jaguars.
articles.body:
The NFL and the National Football League Players Association released a joint statement Sunday revealing there will be an investigation into how the Philadelphia Eagles handled Jalen Hurts' blood clot situation during and around the team's Week 5 trip to London to play the Jacksonville Jaguars.

"The NFL and NFL Players Association are working together to review the matter," the statement said.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported further on the situation and said, "The communication is underway regarding the investigation that the union called for into how this was handled with Hurts. It's taking some time, this is a big endeavor, obviously. But the sides have begun the communication to figure out the logistics of how this is going to happen."

This comes after the NFLPA released a statement Tuesday calling for a "full investigation" into the situation.

"The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the statement said, per ESPN's Tim McManus . "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred. Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward."

McManus noted that statement was in response to comments from NFL chief medical officer Allen Sills that said, "The notion that there's external factors that any of our physicians would put a player in harm's way—that's nonsense."

Sills also called the Eagles' treatment of Hurts "very conservative, very patient-focused and appropriately guarded in every step."

The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released a joint statement as well that said, in part, the quarterback was "clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. … Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery.

"We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."

As McManus detailed, the team said an Oct. 10 ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot and that the team's medical staff and London-based doctors concluded he could safely take the field.

However, a follow-up ultrasound after he returned to Philadelphia showed the blood clot had moved. He was ruled out for the following game against the Carolina Panthers and is expected to miss the remainder of the season.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport (h/t McManus) reported Hurts was able to sleep prior to the Jaguars game after he was in the hospital late into the night.

The Jaguars ended up winning the game 19-17 with a last-second field goal, and Hurts went 21-of-40 for 220 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions.

Tanner McKee played the following game for Philadelphia, which Carolina won 25-14. The Eagles face the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7.

articles.title: Peyton Manning reportedly has no interest in Colts' vacant GM position
articles.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Famer was immediately floated as a potential replacement for Chris Ballard after Ballard was fired.
articles.body:
It looks like we can rule out the possibility of Peyton Manning becoming the Indianapolis Colts' new general manager.

ESPN reported Sunday morning the Colts have "not approached Manning about their vacant GM job, nor would the Hall of Fame quarterback be expected to be interested in the position." The Colts became the first NFL team to change general managers in 2026 when they fired Chris Ballard on Monday after a home loss to the Tennessee Titans.

The idea of the former Colts QB rejoining the organization was first publicly floated by former ESPN anchor Dan Patrick on his radio show immediately after Ballard was fired.

"And I had a source last hour, once this news broke with Chris Ballard, saying that he believes the Irsay [family] will reach out to Peyton Manning about being a GM, maybe the entry point of also having part ownership," Patrick said.

"I know that Peyton and family are happy in Colorado, he has a son who's playing high school football there. But is this enough potential to be an owner of the Colts? Is that enough to kind of lure him back to the NFL?"

The Colts dropped to 2-4 after the loss to the Titans and in the statement announcing Ballard's firing, team CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon said that the team's standard was "to compete for championships."

Ballard became the team's general manager ahead of the 2017 season. During his tenure, the Colts never won the AFC South and made two playoff appearances. The franchise faces a potential decision at quarterback given Daniel Jones' play as he returns from the Achilles injury he suffered in 2025 and the structure of his contract. And the Colts also don't have a first-round pick in the loaded 2027 NFL Draft after trading it to the New York Jets as part of a midseason trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year.

A move into the front office by a retired franchise icon is not without recent precedent. Longtime Atlanta Falcons QB Matt Ryan is in his first season as the team's president of football after working as an analyst for CBS' NFL coverage.

But Manning taking a similar job with the Colts would be an abrupt shift from his current post-playing career. Manning is still an omnipresent corporate pitchman during Sunday commercial breaks and regularly hosts the Manningcast alternate "Monday Night Football" broadcast with his brother Eli.

If the two-time Super Bowl champion ever wants to work for an NFL team, he'll have no shortage of suitors. But it clearly doesn't seem that a reunion with the Colts is in the immediate offing.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers met his wife in 2017; how his romances with Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley fit into the story
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers says he met his now-wife in 2017 and knew he wanted to be with her.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers says he met his now-wife in 2017 and knew he wanted to be with her. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback, 42, has laid out that timeline on two podcasts this year. It changes how his relationships with Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley read in hindsight. It also pulled a public response from another ex, Mallory Edens. Rodgers confirmed in June 2025 that he had married his wife, Brittani, but most of the years between that first meeting and the wedding were spent with other people.Aaron Rodgers met his wife in 2017On The Pat McAfee Show on March 4, Aaron Rodgers said they did not date back then, and that she soon "moved back across the pond." He did not say which month they met.Distance did the rest.Later, on Not Just Football with Cam Heyward, he went further. He said he was "emotionally unavailable" for seven or eight years after meeting her, and that he put everything into football while an ocean separated them. It is a striking thing to say about a stretch that included two very public relationships and one very public engagement.By 2024, Rodgers had reconnected with Brittani, and they eloped in 2025. He said the wedding took place a couple of months before he confirmed it. She stays out of view, which is a sharp contrast to his earlier love life. In July 2025 he told Sports Illustrated she was "the right one," and he credits her with helping him open up to repairing his relationships with his estranged family.How Danica Patrick and Shailene Woodley fit the timelinePatrick came first. She confirmed in January 2018 that she was dating Rodgers, and the two appeared together at the Daytona 500 the next month. They had first met at the ESPYS in 2012. From the outside it looked picture-perfect, with shared photos and romantic getaways.Rodgers now tells it differently. On the Heyward podcast he claimed there was no intimacy at all with Patrick. That is his account only. Patrick's side is not part of this coverage.Woodley's story moved faster and quieter. The engagement became public when Rodgers mentioned it in an interview in February 2021, and People then confirmed she was the woman involved. They ended the engagement in 2022. Rodgers has since alleged that Woodley gave him an ultimatum before their planned marriage. Again, only one side is on the record.Then there is Edens. She and Rodgers were linked in early 2023 after being seen courtside at Bucks games. When his comments surfaced, she answered on Instagram while promoting her film Charlie Harper, joking that her ex was on a press tour saying he never loved anyone he dated after 2017.That reply matters because it shows how this story is being built. Rodgers is rewriting a decade of his private life years after the fact, and the people in it are not agreeing to the edit. Patrick and Woodley have not publicly answered. Edens did, and she did it with a joke.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL overcomes civil unrest, Trump concerns and calls to postpone as Steelers and Saints kick off in Paris
articles.summary: The NFL kicked off at Stade de France despite Paris protests and calls from Trump to postpone the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints game.
articles.body: After the wisdom of America's most popular sport was questioned over its insistence to play its first-ever game in France in the wake of a Saturday filled with protests and violence, the NFL kicked off inside Paris's Stade de France on Sunday. So, we've learned a lesson: The league that played the fabled Ice Bowl in temperatures of minus-13°F, played the Fog Bowl in zero visibility, and played Super Bowl XXIII just days after riots in Miami, has a new a benchmark for playing despite difficult circumstances. Surrounded by a heavier security presence than perhaps any NFL regular-season game before, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints kicked off just as the league planned for months at around 2:30 p.m. Paris time (9:30 a.m ET in the United States). NEARLY 1,000 ARRESTED ACROSS FRANCE AS POLICE FIND POTENTIAL WEAPONS ON PROTESTORS: OFFICIALS The game is being played in the wake of an exhausting Saturday in which a government estimated 110,000 protesters consisting of students, workers, farmers, socialists, communists, pro-Palestine Muslims, anarchists, Antifa and other radicals took to the streets to march, battle police, and cause civil unrest. And although that unrest forced the shuttering of Saturday's three official fan events planned by the NFL, Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints, it didn't claim Sunday's game. Stade de France, approximately nine miles north of the Eiffel Tower, was near capacity at kickoff. It is unknown if the game has faced any credible security threats prior to kickoff. Emails to the league's security department and the Prefecture de Police de Paris have not been answered by publication time. And while the teams and players will tell the tale of this game, the story of how it remained as scheduled despite the surrounding violence is an equally compelling and perhaps controversial narrative. FRANCE'S TOP SOCCER TEAM OBEYS POLICE ORDER TO MOVE SUNDAY MATCH; SAINTS, STEELERS OWNERS MEET WITH MACRON The NFL is playing this first game in France after calls from pundits, at least one player's wife, and even the President of the United States to postpone or relocate. Paris Saint-Germaine rescheduled its Saturday match to Monday because of the unrest and that fed the chorus of voices calling for the NFL to do the same. But when asked by OutKick if it still expected to play the game amid the postponement of the soccer match and the shuttering of its own pregame fan events, the NFL had a one word answer: "Yes." The NFL reached that decision even though President Donald Trump admitted he was "worried about it," and went on to admit, "I would've said the NFL could've probably postponed that match, if you want to know the truth." The NFL faced similar calls to back down throughout the past week. NFL MONITORS FRANCE STREET VIOLENCE BEFORE SAINTS-STEELERS GAME NEAR PA RIS WITH A MAJOR DECISION LOOMING But the week was filled with the league officials saying they were moving ahead with the game, with the understanding it had contingencies for doing something else if necessary. NFL executive vice president for Club Business and International Peter O'Reilly said last week the league was being "vigilant" about the situation in France but still confident the game would go forward. "We've got confidence in the plans both from an ops and security standpoint," he said. That confidence was echoed by Commissioner Roger Goodell, who informed reporters that he had been in contact not just with the U.S. Department of State but with Secretary of State Marco Rubio himself. EXCLUSIVE: SECRETARY OF STATE MARCO RUBIO GIVES NFL COMMISSIONER ROGER GOODELL ASSURANCES ABOUT PLAYING IN FRANCE Rubio confirmed to OutKick that the U.S. Embassy and France believed the game would "be fine." The intriguing thing about this game and the NFL's recent misadventure in London, where Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts flew approximately 11 hours roundtrip while battling a blood clot that got worse after the return flight home, is that more players have openly questioned the league's embrace of international games. Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf was asked in France if there is a country he would like to play a next international game? "No, sir," Metcalf said, "because I really don't like traveling outside the U.S. to play football." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Roger Goodell Addresses NFL International Expansion Team and Paris Game Future
articles.summary: The NFL has made its presence known in international markets with a number of games, but a team outside the United States is still on commissioner Roger Goodell's radar.
articles.body:
The NFL has made its presence known in international markets with a number of games, but a team outside the United States is still on commissioner Roger Goodell's radar.

He said Sunday it remains "likely" there will be an international NFL franchise, although he did not provide a timeline or location, per NFL reporter Joe Browne .

Goodell also said there was "zero doubt" ahead of Sunday's game between the New Orleans Saints and Pittsburgh Steelers the league would return to Paris for another contest.

NFL House in Paris Closes for Protests (AP)

International games were a major focus of the 2026 season, as the NFL scheduled a record nine of them in Melbourne (Australia), Rio de Janeiro (Brazil), London (U.K.), Paris (France), Madrid (Spain), Munich (Germany) and Mexico City (Mexico).

In fact, the league ushered in the new campaign with the opening game between the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Sunday's contest between the Saints and the Steelers comes after three straight games in London, two of which featured the Jacksonville Jaguars playing back-to-back against the Philadelphia Eagles and Houston Texans.

Next up is a Week 9 game between the Cincinnati Bengals and Atlanta Falcons.

Still, having one-off games, even as many as there are this season, in international markets is much different than having an actual team playing overseas. The travel logistics for that team would be challenging, as it would have to take a long flight for every road game if it was located in Europe.

A team in Canada or Mexico would mitigate some of those concerns.

Still, Goodell didn't give a location or timeline, suggesting there likely won't be a team based in an international market in the immediate future.

For now, the focus seems to be on the international games and expanding into different markets. The commissioner said the league would be back in Paris, and Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated reported Wednesday that the league could go to Tokyo as soon as 2028 with an eye on other locations as well.

"As for other new frontiers, some teams love the idea of going to Italy next, but that may not happen until new stadiums open in Milan (2030) and Rome (2031), ahead of the 2032 Euros," he wrote. "Then there's the idea the NFL's Peter O'Reilly raised of playing in new cities in countries the league's already been to, like potentially Manchester in the U.K., Barcelona (which has a stadium under renovation) in Spain, or Sydney in Australia."

It's clear the NFL will continue to focus on the international markets, and that could eventually result in a team being based outside of the country.

articles.title: Unique national anthem ahead of NFL Paris game between Steelers and Saints draws mixed reviews
articles.summary: The Soul Rebels' jazz national anthem before the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints game in Paris divided fans with its brass-band style.
articles.body: The NFL brought its own French flair to the pregame festivities ahead of the kickoff between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints in Paris on Sunday, which predictably resulted in a mixed reaction. After both teams took the field at Stade de France, The Soul Rebels, an eight-piece brass ensemble, played a unique rendition of "The Star-Spangled Banner." It was far from the typical version of the national anthem that fans are accustomed to hearing ahead of contests, but the jazz-style rendition made sense with the French influence on the city of New Orleans, which is where the brass band is originally from. The Soul Rebels released a new song in the days leading up to the game and their performance in Paris, appropriately titled 'Saints in Paris.' According to NOLA, the band will take the stage on the sideline to perform at the end of each quarter. The group also performed during pre-game festivities ahead of Super Bowl LIX in 2025 in New Orleans. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! With the national anthem being a bit more upbeat and entirely instrumental, some fans tuning in loved what they heard, while others, not so much. "A New Orleans brass band doing the anthem in Paris is a perfect touch, The Soul Rebels delivered," one user wrote on X. "Whoever's idea that was, give them a raise," another fan wrote. "We might have a new worst national anthem," a user wrote with a crying-laughing emoji. Another negative review simply read, "It was a - -." NFL OVERCOMES CIVIL UNREST, TRUMP CONCERNS AND CALLS TO POSTPONE AS STEELERS AND SAINTS KICK OFF IN PARIS While the game between the Steelers and Saints got off to a smooth start, the civil unrest in and around Paris continues to be one of the biggest stories around the globe. articles.title: Is Josh Jacobs going to play today? Packers RB Week 7 status revealed
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has missed the first six games of the season. Is he playing in Week 7?
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers are getting back one of their top offensive playmakers – for now.

Running back Josh Jacobs was removed from the commissioner's exempt list after Week 6, and the Packers officially activated him on Saturday, Oct. 24. The running back is still under league investigation for a domestic violence incident involving his ex-girlfriend earlier this year. He could miss additional games due to an official suspension pending the results of the investigation.

Until the investigation is complete and a punishment has been issued, Jacobs is eligible to play. If the NFL issues a six-game suspension – in line with its policy on domestic violence cases – Jacobs' six games on the commissioner's exempt list would count toward it retroactively. He would not have to miss more games.

Revisit Josh Jacobs' football career amid league uncertainty after arrest

In the meantime, Jacobs returns to a Packers offense that has struggled to move the ball on the ground. Green Bay ranks dead last in rushing yards per game (59.8) and is 31st in rushing success rate (32.5%) through six weeks.

The Detroit Lions are a solid first test as Jacobs and the Packers' Week 7 opponent. They've allowed 107 rushing yards per game (15th in the NFL) and a rushing success rate of 38.4% (13th).

Here's what to know about Jacobs in Week 7:

Yes, Jacobs is active for the Packers' Week 7 game against the Lions.

Jacobs spent the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner's exempt list as the league investigated the running back following his arrest and misdemeanor charges stemming from a domestic dispute with his ex-girlfriend. The NFL announced in a statement last week that it was removing Jacobs from the exempt list on Monday, Oct. 19.

The six weeks the veteran spent on the exempt list match the length of a standard suspension for a domestic violence case, according to the collective bargaining agreement between the NFL and NFLPA. Jacobs' time spent on the exempt list can count towards a possible suspension retroactively, if the league decides to impose one.

The league is seeking to obtain video evidence of the altercation between Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend to determine its severity. If the NFL decides to move forward without the video or is unable to obtain it, that could impact the decision on the length of any future suspension.

Josh Jacobs update: Latest news from court case

Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property during a court appearance on Thursday, Sept. 10 .

As part of an announced plea deal, the 28-year-old was found guilty on the charge of battery and ordered to pay a $1,000 fine plus costs.

For the second charge of criminal damage to property, Jacobs reached a deferred judgment agreement. He will have to meet a list of conditions for the next 12 months in order to have that charge dismissed by the state: no further criminal acts, no contact with the victim, supervision, counseling and restitution payment to the victim.

The presiding judge temporarily sealed the evidence from the case on Sept. 10 after Jacobs' no-contest plea.

On Tuesday, Sept. 15, attorneys representing Jacobs' ex-girlfriend, who is not identified by name in court documents, filed a motion to permanently seal the evidence and discovery materials. If approved, the motion could have prevented the NFL from reviewing surveillance camera footage of the incident as part of its investigation into Jacobs. NFL Media insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report that the league requested access to the video.

On Thursday, Sept. 17, the judge rejected the proposed order to seal the evidence, with online court records citing "improper format." At a follow-up hearing on Sept. 24, the Brown County Court Judge lifted a temporary order that sealed records in the case.

On Wednesday, Oct. 14, Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend each filed injunctions against the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department in an attempt to stop police from releasing the video to the public. Jacobs wants a protective order to permanently seal all records in the case, while his ex-girlfriend wants to restrict only video and other information that could potentially identify her.

Jacobs' ex-girlfriend's attorneys have argued that the sealing of evidence is within her rights under Marsy's Law – a recently added amendment to Wisconsin's state constitution that gives additional rights to victims of a crime – to protect privacy, dignity and safety.

With Jacobs back in action in Week 7, the rest of the Packers' running backs slide down one spot on the depth chart. NFL Media insider Mike Garafolo reported on Oct. 25 that Jacobs "is going to get what would be a normal allotment of reps for a starter."

Through six weeks without Jacobs, Lloyd leads the Packers with his 48 carries, 122 yards and two touchdowns. Johnson is second on the team with 28 carries and 104 yards.

USA TODAY Sports' Nick Brinkerhoff and Danielle Lerner contributed to this report.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers, Steelers trolled for ‘Peaky Blinders’ NFL Paris game fit
articles.summary: Pittsburgh's social team is getting brutally fact-checked for its reference to the hit Netflix show.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers are playing their first-ever NFL game in Paris, but there's some confusion within the franchise about where the matchup is actually taking place.

Pittsburgh's entering the France trip with a 4-2 record and a chance to pick up another win. However, Rodgers and some of his teammates are getting ripped online for their pregame outfit choices.

The Steelers' social media team dropped a "Peaky Blinders" caption while showing off the Pittsburgh QB1 and several other teammates in their dapper attire. The problem is that Mike McCarthy's team isn't playing in England, where the hit Netflix show takes place.

Now, Rodgers and Co. deserve credit for pulling off the impressive look with their expensive suits and flat caps. The fashion statement isn't stopping internet trolls from destroying the team in the comments section.

Steelers' social post makes hilarious mistake

The Steelers are likely more worried about what's happening on the gridiron in Week 7 against the New Orleans Saints. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh's viral post has certainly drawn added attention to the team from an international audience.

Paris is hosting its first NFL game as the league continues its push for global saturation with professional football. The English and "Peaky Blinders" fans don't seem to be taking too kindly to the Steelers' blunder, though.

The Netflix show is set in Birmingham, England following World War 1. The program's supporters are certainly making that clear online. Netflix's popular show lasted six seasons following along the Peaky Blinders criminal gang and their battles in the United Kingdom's streets.

Some of the remarks are quite funny, especially those clever enough to put the situation into American terms.

The Steelers return home for a Week 8 showdown with the Cleveland Browns before getting rest on their bye week. Pittsburgh hopes to re-enter America with its fifth win of the NFL season.
